newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp- firmer dollar seems more appropriate.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp- firmer dollar seems more appropriate.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp believes a firmer dollar might seem more appropriate, a spokesman for the regional state central bank of Hamburg, Mecklenburg and Schleswig-Holstein said on Tuesday.
"A firmer U.S. dollar might seem more appropriate," the spokesman quoted Krupp as telling a news agency in an interview.
The spokesman also said Krupp said in the interview that the Bundesbank would consider cutting German interest rates again if the economy were to falter.
But the spokesman said Krupp believed the Bundesbank would not have a reason to cut rates if current projections for 1996 economic growth were confirmed.

In addition, Krupp said in the interview there was no reason to change rates at the moment since inflation was not a concern and long-term interest rates were satisfactory, according to the regional central bank spokesman.
